sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della situazione geopolitica tesa tra Iran e Israele, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è salito al 21.59, mentre l'S&P 500 ha guadagnato il 2.51%. L'aumento del prezzo del petrolio (BRENT +4.06%) e la debolezza del DXY (-0.02%) contribuiscono a questo sentiment.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the tense geopolitical situation between Iran and Israel, negatively impacting equity markets and increasing demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX rose to 21.59, while the S&P 500 gained 2.51%. The increase in oil prices (BRENT +4.06%) and the weakness of the DXY (-0.02%) contribute to this sentiment.

market_impact_summary.en: The geopolitical situation continues to impact markets. The S&P 500 gained 2.51%, while the VIX rose to 21.59. Oil prices increased by 4.06% (BRENT to $98.60). The DXY fell by 0.02% to 99.01. Gold rose by 0.32% to $4764.80. US 10-year bond yields fell by 1.20% to 4.29%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con risultati misti. Il Nikkei ha perso lo 0,73% a 55,895, mentre lo Shanghai ha guadagnato il 2,69% a 3995,00. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in calo dello 0,54% a 25,752. Questi risultati potrebbero influenzare l'apertura dei mercati europei.

La giornata di oggi si apre con un sentiment di risk-off. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso la seduta precedente con un guadagno del 2,51% a 6782,81. Il Dollar Index (DXY) è sceso dello 0,02% a 99,01, mentre l'euro/dollaro è sceso dello 0,06% a 1,16. Il VIX, indice della volatilità, è salito del 2,61% a 21,59. I tassi di interesse sono in calo, con il TLT Bond USA 20Y che è salito dello 0,32% a 86,92 e il US 10Y Yield che è sceso dell'1,20% a 4,29%. L'oro è salito dello 0,32% a $4764,80 l'oncia.

La situazione geopolitica rimane tesa, con la guerra tra Iran e Israele che continua a preoccupare. La Nato ha espresso la sua preoccupazione per la situazione e ha discusso possibili risposte. L'Unione Europea ha avvertito che potrebbe essere colpita da uno shock stagflazionistico.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, gli Stati Uniti hanno rilasciato recentemente dati non recenti sul PIL, sull'inflazione e sui tassi di interesse. Il tasso Fed Funds è attualmente compreso tra il 3,50% e il 3,75%. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati, con il tasso di deposito al 2,00%. Il prossimo dato importante sarà il PIL QoQ USA, che sarà rilasciato il 29 aprile.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo con il deep dive su Bitcoin. La recente performance di prezzo ha subito una correzione, con BTC che si attesta a $71,205, in calo dell'0.58%. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso netto di $-93.9M, segnale di un sentiment negativo tra gli investitori istituzionali. Tecnicamente, il prezzo di Bitcoin si trova in una fase di consolidamento, con livelli di supporto e resistenza che continuano a essere monitorati dagli analisti.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum, Solana e Binance Coin (BNB) hanno tutte registrato cali nelle ultime 24 ore. Ethereum si attesta a $2,186, in calo del 2.75%, mentre Solana e BNB sono rispettivamente a $82.31 e $602.58, con cali del 2.85% e 1.62%. Questi movimenti sono in linea con la tendenza generale del mercato crypto, che sembra essere influenzata dalle preoccupazioni macroeconomiche e geopolitiche.

L'indice di Fear & Greed è sceso a 14, livello di Extreme Fear, suggerendo che gli investitori sono sempre più cauti e prudenti nelle loro decisioni di investimento. La correlazione con i mercati macroeconomici è evidente, con le notizie relative alle tensioni geopolitiche e alle decisioni delle banche centrali che continuano a influenzare il sentiment degli investitori. In particolare, le recenti dichiarazioni della Fed e le notizie relative all'uso di criptovalute per le transazioni internazionali hanno contribuito a creare un clima di incertezza nel mercato.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off today, as indicated by the mixed performance across various asset classes. The VIX index is up, suggesting increased uncertainty and risk aversion.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. The S&P 500 gained 2.51% on the last close, while the STOXX 600 declined by 0.75%. The Nikkei and Hang Seng indices also experienced losses, down 0.73% and 0.54%, respectively. In contrast, the Shanghai index bucked the trend, rising 2.69%. In the bond market, U.S. 10-year yields decreased by 1.20%, to 4.29%, while the TLT Bond USA 20Y gained 0.32%. The dollar index (DXY) edged down 0.02%, to 99.01, and the EUR/USD pair slipped 0.06%, to 1.16. Commodities saw Brent crude surging 4.06%, to $98.60, and gold prices increasing 0.32%, to $4764.80 per ounce.

On the macroeconomic front, attention is focused on the ongoing tensions in the Middle East, with the Iran war sparking concerns about energy supplies and inflation. Fed officials are reportedly divided on how to respond to the energy surge. In Europe, ECB officials, including Christine Lagarde and Philip R. Lane, are discussing policy responses to the current economic challenges. The EU is warned about a potential 'stagflationary shock.' Additionally, there are concerns about the dollar's weakness and its implications for global markets.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 

The recent Fed minutes suggest that there could be further rate cuts on the horizon, especially with the ongoing situation in Iran. This has had a mixed impact on the crypto space. 

Starting with Bitcoin, we see that the BTC ETF daily net inflow was $-93.9M, indicating some outflows. The price of Bitcoin is currently at $71,205, down 0.58% from the previous day. 

In our BTC deep dive, it's worth noting that despite the short-term price movements, the overall sentiment around Bitcoin remains cautiously optimistic. The recent developments with Iran and potential rate cuts could play a significant role in shaping the future price action.

Moving on to altcoins, we see that Ethereum is down 2.75% at $2,186, Solana at $82.31, down 2.85%, and BNB at $602.58, down 1.62%. The altcoin market is experiencing a bit of a downturn, likely influenced by the same factors affecting Bitcoin.

Lastly, looking at sentiment and fear/greed, the Fear & Greed Index is at 14, indicating extreme fear. This could potentially signal a buying opportunity for some investors. However, it's essential to keep in mind that the crypto market can be highly unpredictable and influenced by a wide range of factors.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with more market insights. Keep an eye on the key events and data releases that could impact your trades. Until then, stay informed and stay ahead. A final word from Prais Alért - see you tomorrow. Have a great day!

articles.title: What is Strategic Rivalry? Why Should We Care?
articles.snippet: The states most likely to draw America into its next major crisis or war are not unknowns. They are the usual suspects: The same handful of states that have threatened the United States repeatedly across decades. Interstate rivals have caused roughly 80 percent of history’s wars and the odds of any given rivalry ending peacefully are little better than a coin toss. Yet America’s key strategy documents since the 2017 National Security Strategy have used phrases like great power competition, interstate strategic competition, and strategic competition without acknowledging the essential difference between a competition and a rivalry. articles.title: Iran’s Asymmetric Counterair Campaign: Attacking the U.S. Air Force’s Nests and Eggs
articles.snippet: On March 27, Iranian drones and missiles struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying an E-3 Sentry, an airborne command center for U.S. operations in the region, and damaging multiple KC-135 tankers. It was not the first strike. Earlier in the month, an Iranian attack had already damaged five KC-135s at the same base. In the history of these aircraft, no enemy had ever achieved such a hit until Iran did both — within two weeks.These strikes are the latest in a broader pattern, part of a deliberate counterair campaign waged through asymmetric means in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. articles.title: The Campaign Ends at the Breach: Lessons from Ukraine on Why Armies Fail
articles.snippet: Somewhere behind the Novodarivka breach point in June 2023, Ukrainian armored formations sat staged and ready. The ammunition was there. The fuel was there. The original concept of operations called for 12 brigades to push through roughly 30 kilometers of frontage, isolate Tokmak within days, and drive south before Russian forces could consolidate. They never moved. The engineers could not open the lane. Without the lane, none of the rest of it mattered.Against prepared defenses, breaching and gap-crossing capacity can decide whether a land force ever gets to test the rest of its campaign design. articles.title: Goldman Cuts Oil Price Forecasts After Ceasefire Announcement
articles.snippet: Goldman Sachs updated its price expectations for crude oil late on Wednesday following the news of a ceasefire deal between Iran and the United States, just hours before reports started coming in suggesting Iran may have closed the Strait of Hormuz again. According to Goldman, the ceasefire would push Brent crude to an average of $90 per barrel in the current quarter, with West Texas Intermediate to $87 per barrel, Reuters reported.
